correctness.rationale: Two distinct distance witnesses for every distinct pair are necessary and sufficient for one landmark erasure. Monotonicity excludes all smaller nonempty sets once each of the 4,368 five-sets fails. A fresh enumeration tested all 8,008 six-sets in each graph and got 448 and 1,600. It reproduced the exact exchange edges, singleton and connected component counts, all eccentricities and entire unordered-distance histograms by exhaustive shortest paths, as well as the orbit lists. Pair counts total 100,128 and 1,279,200 in the connected cases. The verified natural group orders are also full: in Shrikhande the stabilizer of 0 acts faithfully on its neighbor cycle C6, since the nine nonneighbors have distinct pairs of neighbors on that cycle. Thus its order is at most 12, and translations give the 192 bound. In rook the local graph is two disjoint triangles, whose automorphism group has order 72; an off-row/off-column vertex is uniquely determined by one neighbor in each triangle. This gives the 1,152 bound, attained by coordinate permutations and interchange. The exact two-replacement assertion is for Shrikhande; it contains all allowed positive moves of budget two there because one-exchange has no edges.
residual_risks: This is a finite proof for named labeled graphs and the specified exchange relation, not a statement about token sliding, general strongly regular graphs or exact two-exchange on rook.

originality.rationale: Two-witness resolution is known as the k=2 metric generator problem, and exchange geometry on this specific canonical pair has been studied for identifying codes. The prior admissible families and distances are demonstrably different; their enumerations do not imply this minimum two-witness census or its exact exchange threshold and metric distinction.
residual_risks: The novelty judgment is for the exact two-witness census and exchange structure, not the notion of fault tolerance or base exchange. Unindexed prior classifications remain possible; a keyword miss is not negative evidence.

value.rationale: These are the canonical contrasting strongly regular graphs with identical (16,6,2,2) parameters and, here, the same optimum landmark count. The sharp contrast between total one-move arrest and full one-move mobility, followed by restoration of connectivity at budget two, shows that these shared parameters do not fix optimum-landmark reconfiguration. The complete distances and orbit data characterize this concrete benchmark without arbitrary graph or move cutoffs.
residual_risks: The distance histograms characterize these two move graphs, not their entire isomorphism types or a general parameter law.
